body.statement: Do there exist universal finite constants \(M>0\) and \(\rho_0>0\) such that, simultaneously for all \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(0<\rho\le\rho_0\), and \((c_{\ell1},c_{\ell2},c_{\ell3})\in[1/2,4]^3\), one has \(\left|u^2C_{\rho,\ell}+1\right|\le M/u^2\), with the same certificate when \(x_{\ell}=0\) or \(z_{\ell}=0\)?
body.justification: This is the unresolved analytic bottleneck: it upgrades exact cancellation to a uniform leading coefficient without dividing by the cancellation product.
body.gap: Existing inverse-Mills bounds do not provide the required common-cutoff mixed derivative over a full coefficient box including both axes.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether the Gaussian bias frontier and its aggregate signed cancellation criterion are uniformly valid for near-plane empirical designs.
